prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a kitchen scene where an upper wooden cabinet on the right is very close to the camera wearer (roughly 0.3–0.6 metres away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach and brightly rendered), a stove and countertop sit in the foreground at about 0.8–1.5 metres, and a person stands to the left of the stove at roughly 1.2–1.8 metres away in front of a background sink and window (~2.0–2.5 metres away). In frame 1, the person stands in right profile facing the counter and looking down rather than toward the camera wearer, while the right-side cabinet partially occludes the wall and range hood behind it. Across frames 2 and 3, the camera wearer turns rapidly to the right toward a doorway and back wall (~2.5–3.0 metres away in the dark hallway on the right of frame 3, with the cabinet and wall frame at ~0.4–0.8 metres on the left and centre), causing the person and most of the stove to pass out of view before the camera turns back left in frames 4 and 5 to show the person at roughly the same distance (~1.3–1.6 metres). The depth map clarifies the continuous 3D separation between the dark, shadowy foreground cabinet and the recessed hallway or kitchen background that are hard to distinguish in the dark RGB regions. However, the depth map is unreliable during the heavy motion blur of frame 2, where the person's silhouette and kitchen appliances blend into smeared, indistinct grey depth planes.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates a few foreground and mid-ground entities within the kitchen: the person standing near the centre-left (~1.2–1.8 metres from the camera wearer), a dishwasher on the far left (~2.5 metres away, mislabelled as an 'oven' in frame 1), a sink behind the person's left (~2.0 metres away, ~0.5 metres from the person), and stove-top items below and in front of the person (~0.8–1.2 metres from the camera wearer, within both the camera wearer's and the person's arm's reach). In frames 1, 4, and 5, the person's mask shows their upper body in right profile facing the counter and stove rather than looking at the camera wearer, with their lower body cropped out of the bottom of the frame and their right arm extending forward in frame 4 over a foreground pan (labelled 'bowl') and beside a kettle and paper towel roll (both labelled 'bottle', ~0.3 metres apart). During the camera wearer's rightward head turn in frames 2 and 3, the person and counter items disappear entirely from the segmentation map. The map clearly delineates the exact boundaries of the person, sink basins, and stove-top cookware against cluttered and dimly lit surroundings in frames 4 and 5 compared to RGB alone. However, it is unreliable during motion blur and under lighting extremes, completely failing to detect the person in frame 2 while misclassifying the bright window as a 'tv', missing all objects in frame 3, and mislabelling the pan, kettle, paper towels, and appliance.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the upper-body skeleton (yellow) and hand keypoints (magenta) of the single person standing roughly 1.2–1.8 metres in front and to the left of the camera wearer, while omitting all background kitchen structures and objects. In frame 1, the facial keypoints (eyes, nose, ears) are positioned to the right of the neck and shoulder line, confirming the person is facing right and tilted downward toward the counter rather than looking at the camera wearer, with magenta hand keypoints clustered near the bottom edge within the person's arm's reach (~0.4–0.5 metres in front of their torso) and the hips and legs occluded below the frame boundary. In frames 4 and 5, after the camera turns back to the left, the skeleton shows the person turned slightly further away (three-quarter rear-right view) with their right arm reaching forward and down toward the stove in frame 4 and retracted closer to the torso in frame 5, though hand keypoints are missing in both frames. This skeletal representation makes the exact joint angles of the person's reaching right arm and downward head orientation immediately apparent despite dark clothing that blends into the background in the RGB frames. However, the pose map is completely unreliable in frames 2 and 3: it detects nothing in the motion-blurred person of frame 2, and it hallucinates an inverted, distorted body skeleton on the vertical door frame and cabinet edge in frame 3 where no person is present.
